items.text: Index › Self-test (new, the kit's self-test as in Current). After a few minutes of play, open it for a report: what the app checked, plus what the device learned (sounds at once, lag, notes skipped). It keeps a black box, so if the page dies the next start offers the report to copy or email. Also reachable at #selftest.

Past scenes is now a scene browser: each scene is kept as a real picture of the stage, shown in a larger grid, and each has an Add to form button that brings it back and keeps it as a new section of the form (the form then plays its sections by itself). Scenes kept before this show their dots.

Sound load is now counted in one place. A mark that is not played (the device is at its limit, or the sound is not running) is no longer drawn as if it were, and the status line says why. The limit starts at 20 sounds on a touch device and 36 on a computer, falls when the device runs late, rises slowly when it is calm, and is remembered per device.
The synth's notes now disconnect when they end, so long sessions do not pile up audio nodes.

If the device takes the sound away (another app, a call, the lock screen) while Battanboo says it is playing, a chip now says so; a tap wakes the sound, and if it stays dead the score is saved and the page comes straight back. Same recovery as Current.
The HUD no longer slides sideways on the iPad: a panel that stops between two positions snaps back, a resize keeps its panel, and the Index drawer cannot scroll sideways.
The HUD button now opens on the panel you used last, also after a reload.
The Colophon lists the ideas, methods, standards and sister tools Battanboo stands on, and says no third-party library is bundled.

A field sound's ring is now a halo built the way Current builds its sound halos: no middle, level, tone and pitch as dots you drag across, next and previous sound, record or redraw a movement, wander, still, More for the length and wet, duplicate at the lower left and take away at the lower right.

The Index drawer is now the index itself, laid out like Current's: the name, devices, Beta and share, an intro, the Codex toolbar, then the sections with icons (Guide first, Colophon last), each one folded, kept, hidden or moved as in Current.
Crowded moments no longer overload the device: at most 36 recorded sounds sound at once, and the oldest fades out when a new one arrives (it clipped and then crashed on the iPad).
The mini pads in a pane no longer cut off their bottom labels when the pane resizes (the drawing kept its old height).
A slider in a pane keeps at least 180 px; when the row cannot give it that, it moves to a row of its own and fills it.
In the MIDI list, a long assignment no longer hides the control's name; the name shows whole and the assignment is shortened to CC and channel (the device is named once, above).

a sustaining sound (rubbed rim, drones) could play forever once a mark landed on it, with nothing left to turn off. Every mark now ends on its own; only a held finger or a field sound sustains, and Hold off lets go of them all.

The share card (the picture shown when the link is shared) follows the layout of the Digital Broadsides: black, the name large at the top left, the line "A visual sequencer that composes with chance over long sonic fields." in yellow, the corner namemark at the top right, a strip of the score itself across the middle, and the CHAMY·XYZ word at the bottom left. Around the words, the marks of the score are scattered and turned, some soft, as on the launch cover.

Field sounds can move on their own. Hold a field sound for its ring and tap Record, then drag it along any path. Let go, and that path becomes a movement whose length you set separately from how fast your hand went: a number of bars, beats or seconds (it starts at 4 bars). It can loop, go back and forth, or play once and stay. Smooth, Simplify and Steps shape it. The path shows as a faint line on the field.

Random movement for field sounds: Wander in the ring, or Random in the sound's settings. The sound drifts in a closed random loop around where it was; New random shape rolls another, Range sets how far (small, medium, wide).

A field sound's ring is now the same halo ring as in Current: a Sound dot that opens its own ring (the pad, or any colour's sound), Settings, Record, Wander, Nudge, and in the lower left Duplicate (a copy beside it with the same sound, settings and movement) and in the lower right Take away.
Clear all moved out of the sound's ring, because it affects every sound: it is a button beside the cube at the bottom of the field. Undo brings the sounds back.

Undo and redo now cover the field too. Putting a sound down, moving it, changing it, taking it away, or Clear all can each be stepped back and forward with the same buttons (and Ctrl or Cmd+Z) as the grid. Before, Clear all on the field had no way back.

Field sounds are no longer one fixed pad. Hold a field sound (or right-click it) for the ring and tap the note (♪): choose its sound (the built-in pad, or the sound of any colour from the Sounds pane, held while you hold), and set its own level, wet, tone and pitch. "New sounds start with this sound" makes it the default; the same choice is in the Sounds pane under Field.
The field has its own room. In the Sounds pane: Dry booth, Small room, Wooden hall, Cathedral, Cave, Open air, and sliders for Size, Decay, Damping and Wet.
Muting the field fades it out over 4 seconds, and unmuting fades it back in, like the speaker. A sweep crosses the M button while it goes.

Hold on the field is the same button as on the grid: the hand at the top right. Touching the field switches it to the closed hand (Hold) by itself, and touching the grid switches it back to the finger; tap it any time to choose one shot or Hold. The crossed infinity button is gone.

Turning Hold off on a field sound left no way to turn it back on, because the sound vanished when you let go. An infinity button with a slash now sits beside the cube whenever Hold is off; tap it to turn Hold on.
On the field, left, near and right stay in the lower corners and middle, and the cube button sits centred just above "near", as big as the icons in the lower right menu.
Wall and Floor are one cube button on the field. The cube shows the face you are looking at (the walls, or the floor) and a dot where you stand; tap it to switch.
Hold and Clear moved onto the sounds. Hold a field sound, or right-click it, for the ring: nudge it, take it away, keep sounds held (the infinity mark), clear all.
The MIDI button is now a MIDI plug symbol in the lower right menu, just under the clock. The text buttons by the stage edge and in the display footer are gone.
The Wall, Floor, Hold and Clear switches on the field are a small quiet strip in the pad's bottom right corner, not a row of big pills. Wall and Floor are icons.
With more than four colours on a phone, the colour swatches beside the pad were 14 px slivers. They are now a two-column grid of real swatches.
The separate Field display is gone. Its controls (what your finger plays, size of the marks, look of the effects) are now at the foot of Dice and air.
Every heads-up display now starts at the top. Before, the ones with less in them floated to the middle and the others sat at the top, with no reason you could see.

MIDI learn now happens on the controls. Tap MIDI (bottom right of every heads-up display) and every control a knob can move gets a coloured shape. Tap a shape, move a knob: its number appears inside. Tap MIDI again and the mappings keep working; tap it again to see them, the unmapped ones left blank. × on a shape unmaps it.

MIDI knows which controller is which. Switch several devices on or off in the learn panel, and two controllers can use the same knob numbers for different things. Mappings made before this still work, from any device.
Form: Movements is now a large heading, and on a wide screen the movements sit in a right-hand column with everything else on the left.
On a very large monitor the heads-up panes stay a centred column instead of stretching edge to edge, so sliders never run the whole width.

A held sound (Rubbed rim, Scraping glass, Sustain, Air, Crack run) could ring forever when Air was above zero, on the grid as well as on the play button, because its first grain was never given a length. Every grain now has one. Muting a colour also silences it at once, so a ringing sound stops when you press M.
The play button on a held sound (Rubbed rim, for one) no longer rings forever. It sounds for about a second and a half, then lets go.

The line across each colour in the Mixer is now that colour's real sound, drawn live: a bell, a pad and a drum each have their own shape, and it follows the level you set. Before, it was one stock wave that only jumped when a note played.

A play button to the left of each colour in the Mixer, the same size as the grid button above it. It sounds that colour at the level it is set to (so mute, solo and the crossfader count), a quick way to hear and balance the levels.
The Dice and air pane and the Sounds pane use wide screens like the Play pane: the Weave controls beside the touch surfaces, and the colour sounds in two columns beside the sound sets.

A MIDI pane in the heads-up display. Connect your controller, press Learn beside any control (the crossfader, volume, tone, air, space, morph, holds, repeat, tempo, the field or any colour's level), move a knob or slider once, and it is mapped. It shows the number of the last control you moved, so you can see what your device sends. One tap sets a MIDI Fighter Twister's 16 knobs to the main controls and the eight colours. Mappings are kept between visits. Needs Chrome on a Mac or a PC (Safari on iPhone and iPad has no MIDI).
The Mixer's MIDI button now opens that pane.

The Play pane fits its space. Wide: the numbers and controls on the left, the four lines stacked on the right, each with more height to move in. Medium: controls on the left and Auto dice on the right, with the four lines as a 2 by 2 below. Narrow: one column with taller lines.
The small type in the Mixer (pad names and values, colour names and percentages) is larger and grows with the screen.
With the field switched off, its held notes stay visible as faint dots over the grid, so you can see where they are, as the grid's marks do when the grid is off. Taps still go to the grid.
Closing the field panel no longer drops the field's held voices. They keep sounding; Clear, or a double-tap on a note, lets them go.

The field's Wall, Floor, Hold and Clear buttons: the lit ones were unreadable (colour clash). They are readable now, smaller, in one row at the bottom middle of the field instead of the top left, and the field's left, low and right words sit above them. The space around the buttons no longer blocks taps on the cells.
In the Mixer's crossfader, the Grid and Field percentages now sit at their own ends of the slider, beside their icons, instead of in the middle.

Every colour has its own sound. With more than four colours, colours 5 to 8 are a drum kit (each row a different drum), a goblet (crystal), a rubbed rim and a spill of shards, so no sound repeats. Colours 1 to 4 stay the grid's four voices, unchanged. Your choice for each colour is now remembered between visits.

In the Sounds pane, each colour has its own chooser. Sounds are grouped (voices of the grid; struck: one hit that rings away; held: sounds while you hold; banks: a different sound on each row), each with a plain line on what it is, and a + to bring in your own.
Reloading with more than four colours left colours 5 to 8 empty in the Mixer and playing colour 1's sound. They come back with their own sounds now.
The crossfader's mode button is now a square icon (Blend, Fade, Free), the same size as M and S.
The coloured line across each Mixer row fades out under the name and the percentage, and the type has a soft dark edge, so both read clearly.

Note names sit in the top-left corner of their cell. The names chooser is a dropdown like the scale and root: No names, Names on the first row, Names on every cell, Names on hover. It no longer changes width.
The two frame grips are now just dots, set the same small distance inside each edge of the frame, with no handle shape behind them. The area you can grab is the same, and invisible.
Each colour row in the Mixer now names its sound next to the number (Synth: pluck, Glass, Drums...), and the name follows when you change the sound.

Wall, Floor, Hold and Clear now sit on the field itself, in its top-left corner, whenever the field is on, so you change the field where you see it. The Field pane keeps who you are touching, the floor pitch, the size of the marks and the look of the effects.
The Free / Blend / Fade buttons at the foot of the Mixer are gone; the mode button beside the crossfader does their job.
The scale, root and note names, which the grid and the field share, moved to the Mixer, on the right of the Free / Blend / Fade / MIDI row.

The grid and field icons sit either side of the crossfader at the top of the Mixer. Tap one and the crossfader goes all the way to that side (that one at 100%, the other away); double-tap either to put it back in the middle. A button to the right of them chooses how the two cross: Blend (both full in the middle), Fade (opposed, 50 and 50 in the middle) or Free (no crossfade).

The A|B crossfader now also sits at the top of the Mixer, the same one as on the tempo bar, with the grid and field percentages in the middle. The colour bars and the Field bar dim as the crossfader turns them down, so you can see why something is quiet.
The Field bar had the same limit as the colour bars (it could only reach what the crossfader let through). It now runs its full length.

The four colour sliders (1 to 4) could not be pulled past about 13%. They were scaled by the A|B crossfader, so with it toward the field the whole slider shrank to what the crossfader let through. They now always run the full length and set the colour's own level; the crossfader still decides how much of it you hear.
Tapping the Field button a second time while the field is in front dismisses the field and returns to the grid.

The rings, blooms and specks sat off to the side of the shapes that made them, in play and in Cinema, more so on a stretched frame. The effects layer was being squeezed to the grid's width; it now keeps its true size, so every effect is centred on its shape.
The play lines (the bars that sweep across the grid) now run on past its edge, across the whole screen, in play and in Cinema, as the rings and blooms do.
The rings and blooms that answer each sound are no longer cut off at the edge of the grid, in play and in Cinema: the effects layer reaches beyond the grid on every side, so they spread out freely.

Cinema. In full screen, after five quiet seconds, the interface fades away and only the shapes, the play lines and the effects remain, on black, with the grid lines running on to the edges of the screen. Move the mouse, touch the screen or press a key and everything comes back (that first touch only wakes it; it plays nothing).

The frame grips now sit on the frame itself, and the frame can be stretched to the full width of a large screen. Full screen no longer inherits a squeezed frame (that made the grid tall and pushed the bars off the screen); it always uses the whole screen.

On a wide screen (900 px and up) a grip sits on each side of the frame. Drag either one to stretch or squeeze the frame (it stays centred, from 640 px up to the full width); double-click for full width; with a grip focused, the arrow keys step it, Home is narrowest and End is full width. The width is remembered.
With the HUD open, tap the Grid or Field button again to close it, or tap the bare background outside the frame (a drag does not close it).
The Weave preset in use is ringed in bright yellow (a border, not a fill).
The opening's shapes are sharp by the time they stop, and it is the interface that comes into focus behind them, from blurred to sharp as it fades in.
No more sideways jump when the real shapes take over: the opening's canvas is now measured from its own box, so on screens with a scrollbar it lines up with the grid exactly.
The shapes leave slowly, quicken as they travel, then land with the bounce (the glide is a little longer, 0.95 s).

The opening is now the shapes that are frosted, not the interface. Until you tap, the interface is completely transparent and the first grid's shapes drift as frosted glass on a dark ground. Tap, and they glide home. Only when every one has stopped does the interface fade in and the real, sharp shapes replace the frosted ones.

The opening shapes now match the grid you actually get. They were drawn from the first grid before your saved work loaded, so a returning player saw a different set land. They are rebuilt from the loaded grid.
The frost is lighter and clearer (less tint, a sharper blur at 16 px), so the interface shows through it as frosted glass instead of reading as plain grey.

Weave. After the playhead has crossed the grid, its lines slide and the notes wrap round (columns for left and right, rows for up and down, rings and spokes on a ring; several play lines slide both ways). Hold the grid button on the tempo bar, and Weave sits at the foot of that panel: Off or On, five presets (Loom, Prime drift, Fibonacci stairs, Ripple, Odd lift), which lines (Weave, Alt, Even, Odd, All), how far (staggered primes, pairs, Fibonacci, repetitions, all at once), how often, and a button back to the written grid. Locked cells stay put.

Slide by hand. In that panel, switch the edge strips to "Slide by hand": the lock strips become arrows. Drag a strip to slide its column, row, ring or spoke (it snaps to the nearest cell), or tap its arrow for one step. Undo takes it back.

The opening screen is frosted glass over the app, with every shape of the first grid drifting slowly in it, as if in a liquid. Tap, and the shapes snap to their places on the grid while the frost clears and the grid and the rest of the interface appear. (With reduced motion the shapes sit still and the change is quick.)

The timeline now writes each movement's name, and what the players do, inside its own stretch of the bar when there is room (a name from 56 px, the players' line from 150 px). On a narrow screen the time left is dropped so the names stay readable.
Arm, in the Form's Clock row. It shows the timeline ("armed · tap to start") without running the clock. The first tap on the timeline starts it; Start, Pause and Reset also clear Arm.
A flyout stays anchored to its button: it hangs down from the button's top when it fits, otherwise it rises from the button's bottom, and it follows the button if the window changes.
